answer: A reef survey market pays agents for measurements at a narrow inlet. Each paid reading cites a signed buoy packet whose sequence number is consumed on settlement; a mirror copy earns nothing from another account. To multiply rewards, an attacker must deploy more buoys, obtain independent packets, and risk losing a bond when random physical inspections find fabricated sites. Wealthy operators can still buy many buoys and inspectors can collude, so inspection assignments rotate and raw signals remain auditable.
